stumbles.quote: Colours are within ΔE76 0.07 of a reference.
stumbles.why: The reference is never identified (a real film measurement? a physical model?), so the claim can't be interpreted or checked. ΔE76 is also jargon for many readers.

stumbles.quote: black film spreads from the top
stumbles.why: Black film isn't explained. Readers who don't know thin-film interference won't see why the film turns black, or that black means very thin and about to pop.
It doesn't say what sinks or rises relative to. It also doesn't say whether tilting the phone sets the gravity direction, so the mechanism is unclear.

This sits oddly beside the 'tilt your phone' prompt. It's unclear whether tilt input works at all, or whether the page only runs on desktop with simulated tilt. The post also doesn't say which browsers support WebGPU.

point: A WebGPU compute soap-film simulation where tilting the phone moves thick film down and thin film up, and the film drains, goes black, and pops, with colours claimed to be accurate to a reference but not tested on a real phone.
